Items.Authors: Daniel Lancaster, Stefan Kraus, Sorabh Chhabra, Jyotirmay Paul, Owain Snaith
Items.Title: Characterisation and testing of the PICSIR integrated optics device and all-in-one beam-combiner of BIFROST
Items.Abstract: BIFROST combines the four beams produced by the Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI) into a spectrograph in the near-infrared (1-1.7um). To combine the light of the four beams it was proposed and contracted to use a integrated optics chip to combine the light of four beams and produce an interferometric signal using the ABCD method. This report details the acceptance testing and methodology used to verify the performance of preliminary test devices. These tests are later then be implemented into the characterising the performance of BIFROST's new all-in-one (AIO) beam combiner. We shall discuss the merits of either system.

Items.Authors: Léonie Sommer, Johannes Müller-Seidlitz, Valentin Emberger, Robert Andritschke, Astrid Mayr, Annika Behrens, Günter Hauser, Peter Lechner, Anna Schweingruber, Jonas Reiffers
Items.Title: Characterisation of operational parameters for the NewAthena WFI DEPFET flight production
Items.Abstract: NewAthena’s Wide Field Imager (WFI) uses detectors made up from Depleted P-Channel Field Effect Transistor (DEPFET) pixels operated in rolling shutter mode. The Large Detector Array (LDA) contains a 2 × 2 array of 512 × 512 pixel Large Detectors (LDs) allowing for a field of view of 40’ × 40’ while the 64 × 64 pixel Fast Detector (FD) can observe very bright X-ray sources due to a faster timing of 2.5 µs per row. We used 64 × 64 pixel testing sensors to analyze the range of the sensor operational parameters and to optimize the ASIC and DEPFET parameters i.e. current and voltage settings, as well as the DEPFET temperature and read out timing parameters, resulting in an improved energy resolution as well as reduced noise and otherwise improved sensor characteristics.

Items.Authors: Annika Behrens, Valentin Emberger, Robert Andritschke
Items.Title: Characterisation of the NewAthena WFI DEPFET detectors’ on-chip optical blocking filter
Items.Abstract: The Wide Field Imager (WFI) will be one of two instruments on the NewAthena X-ray observatory. Using Depleted P-channel Field Effect Transistor (DEPFET) sensors, it will provide imaging spectroscopy with a large field of view of 40’ x 40’ and near fano-limited energy resolution over a broad energy band from 0.2 keV to 15 keV. The DEPFET sensors are however also sensitive to optical and UV light, which necessitates the use of an optical blocking filter (OBF). WFI will employ both an external filter and an on-chip filter consisting of 90 nm of aluminium deposited directly on the DEPFET sensors. We have investigated the homogeneity and the attenuation of the on-chip OBF at varying wavelengths from UV to infrared.

Items.Authors: Remon van Gaalen, Maria Bergomi, Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Luca Marafatto, Silvio di Rosa, Marco Dima, Gabriele Umbriaco, Davide Greggio, Tânia Sofia Gomes Machado, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Tom Herbst
Items.Title: Characterising a novel 8k sCMOS detector for on-sky operations with LBT’s new speckle imager
Items.Abstract: For the new speckle imager for the Large Binocular Telescope, NirvanaVIS, a novel detector has been selected, the Teledyne COSMOS-8k.  Detector performance has a large influence on the performance of the speckle holography deconvolution method envisioned for this instrument. Which benefits from a detector that has a large array of pixels, with a fast readout that can operate in a global shutter mode, like the selected COSMOS-8k.  As NirvanaVIS will utilise the on-sky proven GLAO correction provided by the LINC-NIRVANA instrument, it will have a fast track to on-sky operations and will arrive at the telescopeat the end of the year. Given that this is one of the first COSMOS-8k cameras to operate on-sky, additional interest goes out to its characterisation.  Here the procedures, processing, and results of the tests performed at the laboratories of INAF-Padova are presented.

Items.Authors: Michael Krumrey, Marcos Bavdaz, Levent Cibik, Robert Fechner, Christian Gollwitzer, Peter Müller, Dieter Skroblin
Items.Title: Characterization of mirrors, filters and detectors for NewAthena and other X-ray missions with monochromatic synchrotron radiation
Items.Abstract: NewAthena will cover the photon energy range from 0.2 keV to 12 keV. The properties of all components (mirrors, filters and detectors) depend on the photon energy. The beamlines in the laboratory of PTB at the synchrotron radiation facility BESSY II in Berlin can cover almost the entire energy range with monochromatic radiation so that also fine structures at the absorption edges of the involved chemical elements (e.g. oxygen, silicon, platinum etc.) can be studied. The measured transmittance of NewAthena filters, reflectance of mirror coatings and transmittance of entire Mirror Modules of the NewAthena Silicon Pore Optics will be shown. Examples will also be given for the characterization of pixelated detectors like pn-CCDs including the determination of the absolute detection efficiency.

Items.Authors: Federico Fiorentino, Ugo Lo Cicero, Luisa Sciortino, Michela Todaro, Edoardo Alaimo, Fabio D'Anca, Alberto Gulizzi, Salvatore Varisco, Claudio Saitta, Marco Barbera
Items.Title: Characterization of pinholes on polyimide-based filters for NewAthena
Items.Abstract: ESA’s large mission NewAthena will employ innovative microcalorimeter detectors to observe the universe in the soft X-Ray with unprecedented energy resolution. To protect the detectors and ensure optimal performance, it will make use of optical blocking filters consisting of a structural layer, for which the current baseline is thin polyimide films, coated with a thin aluminum layer. In this work, we present the study and characterization of pinholes in filters consisting of a thin (30 nm or 70 nm) Al layer on top of polyimide layers of various thickness (45 to 150 nm). Optical microscopy in correlation with IR spectroscopy is used to estimate the pinhole distributions and sizes, and the impact on the filter performance.

Items.Authors: Guido Torrioli, Paolo Bastia, Giovanni Benevento, Fabio Chiarello, Artur Coimbra, Matteo D'Andrea, Luca Giganti, Giacomo Gorla, Claudio Macculi, Luigi Piro, Francesco Villa
Items.Title: Characterization of the Cryogenic AntiCoincidence detector (CryoAC) warm electronics breadboard for the X-IFU Athena instrument
Items.Abstract: ATHENA is an X-ray astrophysics observatory selected as a large-class ESA mission. It features a large-area telescope feeding two focal-plane instruments: the X-ray Integral Field Unit (X-IFU) and the Wide Field Imager. The X-IFU is a cryogenic spectrometer based on a ~1500-pixel TES array operating at 50 mK to provide high-resolution, spatially resolved spectroscopy. Since the TES array cannot distinguish science photons from background particles, the instrument includes the Cryogenic AntiCoincidence detector (CryoAC), which rejects events detected simultaneously in both systems, significantly reducing the instrumental background. The CryoAC consists of four TES-based pixels read out by SQUIDs at 50 mK in a Flux Locked Loop configuration. Its warm electronics include the analog WFEE, implementing the FLL, and the WBEE, which digitizes and processes signals through an FPGA-based event-identification algorithm. This work presents tests on a breadboard implementation of the warm electron

Items.Authors: Xavier Haubois, Robert G. van Holstein, Pierre Bourget, Nicolas Schuhler
Items.Title: Characterization of the instrumental polarization of VLTI/ATs
Items.Abstract: The Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI) provides unique capabilities for high-angular-resolution observations at milliarcsecond scales.  Combined with polarimetric capabilities of sufficient accuracy, great enhancement is to be expected in the study the study of circumstellar environments and young stellar objects, to name a few. With this talk, we present a characterization of polarization properties obtained with the ATs.  This work addresses the description of the polarimetric measurements, the estimation of the instrumental polarization arising from ATs and beam train optics, and propsect for extracting astrophysically polarized signals. This characterization provides the foundation for exploiting VLTI/AT's polarimetric capabilities for science applications and identifies paths for future improvements to the facility's polarimetric calibration.

Items.Authors: Ashley D. Baker, Jake Zimmer, Timothee Greffe, Elijah Anakalea-Buckley, Don Neill, Michael Langmayr, David Hale, Prakriti Gupta, Nemanja Jovanovic, Ricardo Meneses, Robert Bertz, Jean-Baptiste Ruffio, David Brearley, Michael Fitzgerald, Dimitri Mawet, Roger Smith, Reston Nash, Samuel Halverson, Rose Gibson, James Brugger, Jeb Bailey, Hector L. Rodriguez, James Wiley
Items.Title: Characterization of the Keck/HISPEC H4RG-10 Detectors and H2RG Tracking Camera
Items.Abstract: HISPEC is a single-mode fiber-fed, stabilized instrument that will be commissioned on the Keck II telescope in 2027. Its science program will focus on NIR spectral characterization of exoplanets and brown dwarfs with the driving requirement of achieving sub meter per second radial velocity precisions. The two HISPEC spectrometers cover yJ and HK bandpasses respectively, each using an H4RG-10 from the Roman project as its detector. HISPEC's front-end instrument, which is responsible for coupling light into the science fibers, utilizes a spare JWST H2RG for its tracking camera. The three detectors were characterized at Caltech in early 2026 before being integrated into the full instrument. Here were provide details on the detector read out electronics, the test setup, the results of the various detector properties measured, and how they relate to the instrument's design and operational requirements as demanded by the HISPEC science program.

Items.Authors: Giacomo Gorla, Claudio Macculi, Matteo D'Andrea, Guido Torrioli, Luigi Piro, Mikko Kiviranta, Achini Rathnathilaka
Items.Title: Characterization of the SQUIDs for the Athena X-IFU Cryogenic AntiCoincidence detector
Items.Abstract: This poster presents the full characterization of the new FAB 4 SQUID amplifiers developed for the CryoAC detector of the Athena X-IFU mission. The study includes voltage–flux (V–Φ) measurements, evaluation of noise performance, gain, and thermal dissipation, as well as a direct comparison with the previous FAB 3 SQUID generation. A detailed analysis of the V–Φ response as a function of the input coil current is reported, highlighting the impact of the detector operating point on the readout chain’s noise behavior. Finally, we present the first-light results of the latest CryoAC Demonstration Model 1.2, operating at 50 mK and equipped with these new SQUID devices.

Items.Authors: Stella Vješnica, Paško Roje, Mike Kretlow, Martin M. Roth, Patrik Kušter
Items.Title: Characterizing the Hamamatsu ORCA-Quest 2 CMOS camera for astronomical applications using laboratory measurements and on-sky time-series observations
Items.Abstract: We report a combined laboratory and on-sky characterization of the Hamamatsu ORCA-Quest 2 scientific CMOS camera, a device widely used in quantum optics experiments but not yet commonly used for astronomical applications. Laboratory measurements at the Deutsches Zentrum für Astrophysik using a calibrated photometric testbench provided conversion gain, readout noise, full-well capacity, dark current, and a wavelength dependent quantum efficiency curve. On-sky time series observations with the 1.23m telescope at Calar Alto Observatory in Spain were used to construct RMS versus magnitude precision curves after differential photometry. Together, these results quantify the detector’s noise behavior and photometric performance, enabling an assessment of its suitability for precision optical astronomy.

Items.Authors: Mauro Dolci, Angelo Valentini, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Piero D'Incecco, Stefano Di Frischia, Matteo Canzari, Enzo Brocato, Simone Benedetti, Fiore De Luise, Amico Di Cianno, Nicola Napoleone, Anna M. Piersimoni, Elisa Portaluri, Gabriella Raimondo, Leonardo Tartaglia, Gaetano Valentini
Items.Title: CI2RCE, the new infrared imager for the Visible-Infrared Telescope at the Campo Imperatore Observatory: from design to installation
Items.Abstract: VIT (Visible-Infrared Telescope) is a 1.1m telescope installed at the Campo Imperatore observing station, in Central Italy, at an elevation of 2200 m a.s.l. For almost 30 years it has been devoted to NIR astronomical imaging over a squared FoV of 19.4 arcmin2. The facility is now being upgraded with a new IR imager, covering more than twice the area FoV (more than 40 arcmin2), and being provided in addition with a seeing-enhancement capability produced by a devoted Tip-Tilt (TT) corrector able to actually provide sharper images. The overall history of the refurbishment program is presented, with emphasis on the results of the integration and test phase, as well as the first light and the on.sky commissioning. A list of potential science cases is presented and discussed.

Items.Authors: Markus Kasper, Laura Schreiber, Emiliano Diolaiti, Silvano Desidera, Oscar Carrión-González, Siddharth Maharana, Arthur Vigan, Gaël Chauvin, Axel Potier, Matthias Tecza, Eric Stadler, Sebastiaan Haffert, Maud Langlois, Silvia Scheithauer, Carlos Correia, Stefan Ströbele, Benjamin Charnay, Emilio Carlo Molinari
Items.Title: Closing the technology gap for the Extremely Large Telescope’s Planetary Camera and Spectrograph (ELT-PCS): description of the roadmap activity
Items.Abstract: PCS is the ELT’s planet imaging camera and spectrograph, designed for direct observation and characterization of exoplanets down to Earth-mass in the habitable zones of M-stars. The PCS R&D roadmap project is a community effort and sets out a strategic plan to define scientific requirements, instrument concept, and to analyze the capabilities and key budgets of the system, such as mass, volume, and throughput. A major goal is identifying critical enabling technologies and advancing their readiness to mitigate risks.  The roadmap also fosters collaborative training for early-career researchers in high-contrast imaging. The project structure consists of seven interdependent work packages: Science Case and Technology Readiness, Coronagraphy and Wavefront Control, Science Instruments, XAO, XAO-DM, Systems Engineering, and Science Yield Analysis. Each is jointly led by community experts. The planned deliverables include a summary white paper to support ELT PCS Phase A approval.

Items.Authors: Sara Svendsen, Sonny Massahi, Desirée Ferreira, Diego Paredes-Sanz, Arne S. Jegers, Finn Christensen, Aniket Thete, Christian Körnig, David Girou, Max Collon, Dieter Skroblin, Levent Cibik, Robert Fechner, Christian Gollwitzer, Michael Krumrey, Marcos Bavdaz
Items.Title: Coating development for the NewAthena X-ray optics
Items.Abstract: The development of X-ray reflective mirror coatings for the NewAthena optics is progressing, with efforts aimed  at achieving the required effective area performance, and ensuring full compatibility with the Silicon Pore Optics  manufacturing processes.  Platinum and carbon coating designs have been demonstrated to be suitable for NewAthena, but several aspects  of thin film quality and stability must still be addressed. Particularly important is the experimental validation  of multilayer coatings, as they are an enabling technology necessary to achieve the effective area requirement for  the high-energy science cases.  We present results of coating development and characterisation of representative thin film coatings using X-ray  reflectometry, stylus profilometry, and atomic force microscopy.

Items.Authors: Marshall C. Johnson, Marcelo Tala Pinto, Jonathan Crass, Brian Sands, Julia Brady, Michael Engelman, Daniel Pappalardo, Mark Derwent, Jackson Datkuliak, Xavier Lesley, Justin R. Crepp, Andrew Bechter, Eric Bechter, Christian Schwab, David Aikens, Chad Bender, Chris Brandon, Cynthia Brooks, Matheus J. Castro, Jeffrey Chilcote, Al Conrad, Gregory Delo, Erin Duell, Matthew Engstrom, Steve Ertel, Louis Fantano, John Keith Feggans, Hali Flores, Scott Gaudi, David King, Ondrej Kitzler, Kaitlin Kratter, Jeffrey Kruk, Thomas Legero, Stanimir Letchev, Jerry Mason, Joaquin Mason, Matthew Misch, Jacob Pember, Richard Pogge, Andreas Quirrenbach, Allie Renshaw, Austin Richie, Alexa Rizika, Nandini Sadagopan, Joshua Schlieder, Sai Vidyud Senthil Nathan, Joseph Shields, Jonathan Shover, Mark Smithwright, James Smous, Jayde Spiegel, Julian Stürmer, Sahil Sura, Robert Switzer, Joe Thomes, Augustyn Waczynski, Ji Wang, Lauren Weiss, Daniel Wilson, Dane Zielinski-Nicolson
Items.Title: Commissioning and on-sky performance verification of iLocater
Items.Abstract: iLocater is a high-resolution near-infrared extreme precision radial velocity (EPRV) spectrograph which is being deployed to the Large Binocular Telescope (LBT) in early 2026. We present the reintegration, commissioning and initial on-sky verification program, including from both a solar feed and night-time observations with the LBT. We detail a series of tests to verify instrument throughput, adaptive optics and single-mode fiber performance, and radial velocity performance.

Items.Authors: Mackenzie R. Lach, Steph Sallum, Andrew Skemer
Items.Title: Commissioning results for the SCALES non-redundant aperture masking mode
Items.Abstract: SCALES stands for “Slicer Combined with Array of Lenslets for Exoplanet Spectroscopy” and is an integral field spectrograph (IFS) at W. M. Keck Observatory that will directly image and spectroscopically characterize circumstellar disks and young exoplanets from 2-5μm, among other scientific targets. SCALES’s low spectral resolution and imaging modes are equipped with a set of complimentary non-redundant aperture masks (NRM), which transform the telescope aperture into an interferometer and allow for improved angular resolution beyond lambda/d at moderate contrasts. We present the first commissioning results from the SCALES NRM mode. We observe several known targets, including bright stars, binaries, and stars with known protoplanetary disks in order to validate the performance of this mode. We compare our observations with prior SCALES simulations.

Items.Authors: Jeffrey C. Mason, Michelle Creech-Eakman, Andres Olivares, Chris Salcido, James Luis
Items.Title: Commissioning the Infrared Coherencing Nearest Neighbor (ICoNN) fringe tracker
Items.Abstract: The Magdalena Ridge Observatory Interferometer (MROI) has recently obtained first fringes using our first science combiner, FOURIER. As subsequent observations obtain fringes on fainter targets, the MROI will soon need a dedicated fringe tracker. The Infrared Coherencing Nearest Neighbor (ICoNN) fringe tracker is the inaugural fringe tracker for the MROI. With the MROI collecting science fringes regularly, and a third telescope scheduled to arrive in about 18 months, ICoNN has become a high priority for the observatory. ICoNN is a fringe tracker which consists of four subsystems: the switchyard, the beam combiner, the periscope optics, and the spectrograph/dewar. ICoNN operates in the H or Ks bands, to complement the scientific observations with FOURIER and maintain maximal throughput. This paper details the commissioning of ICoNN as it is upgraded to a new detector and all subsystems are integrated, tested, and deployed on sky.

Items.Authors: Yu Zhou, Jiao Ding, Ryota Hayakawa, Tommaso Ghigna, Kaori Hattori
Items.Title: Comprehensive Microstructural and Superconducting Characterization of AlMn Transition-Edge Sensors: Effects of Annealing, Interface Roughness, and Proximity to Nb Leads
Items.Abstract: Superconducting Transition-Edge Sensors (TESs) using AlMn films are promising for high-resolution cryogenic detectors in future astronomy missions due to their tunable critical temperature (T_c). This study systematically examines how thermal processing—specifically annealing temperature and baking conditions—affects T_c, interface roughness, and microscopic film properties. Using current–voltage characteristics, critical current–temperature relations, coherence-length analysis, and microstructural measurements, we establish direct links between processing parameters, surface morphology, and superconducting behavior. We also quantify proximity effects from Nb leads and their influence on the AlMn transition. Our results show that thermal treatments not only tune T_c but also drive significant microstructural changes that impact device performance. These findings provide guidance for optimizing fabrication protocols for high-performance AlMn TES arrays in next-generation instruments.

Items.Authors: Flavia Calderone, Isabella Pagano, Simonetta Chinellato, Valentina Viotto, Demetrio Magrin, Jacopo Farinato, Matteo Munari, Francesco Borsa, Roberto Ragazzoni, Daniele Brienza, Raffaele Piazzolla, Mario Salatti, Elisabetta Tommasi, Duncan Goulty, Joseph Huesler, Virginie Cessa, Alexis Brandeker, Emanuele Capuano, Emanuele Alberto Macrì, Giammarco Roini, Marco Nebiolo, Donata Valletti
Items.Title: Configuration management activities for the PLATO telescope optical units
Items.Abstract: ESA’s PLATO (PLAnetary Transits and Oscillations of stars) M3-class mission is designed to detect and characterise exoplanets orbiting the habitable zone of solar-type stars through high-precision photometric observations. Its payload contains an array of 26 Telescope Optical Units (TOUs), each one part of a multi-camera system optimised for high photometric stability and wide-field sky coverage. During the TOUs development and production phase, which has involved contributions from multiple institutes and industrial partners, Configuration Management (CM) has contributed to ensure design integrity, traceability and consistency between manufactured items and documentation throughout the design, development, AIT/AIV and lifecycle phases of the units. The main CM activities applicable to space products and their application to the PLATO TOUs, performed by INAF in compliance with the ECSS standards, are here outlined with a specific focus on the Document Configuration and Data Management.

Items.Authors: Pierre Vermot, Damien Gratadour, Paul Fontanillas, Jordan Raffard
Items.Title: Convolutional neural networks for pyramid wavefront sensing
Items.Abstract: I present an architecture and training strategy to reconstruct atmospheric residual phase in an arbitrary modal basis using a pyramid wavefront sensor (pWFS). While standard linear reconstruction works well in high-SNR linear regimes, strong residual phase exposes the pWFS’s intrinsic non-linearity and limits performance. Modulation can extend the linear range but reduces sensitivity. Although neural networks underperform in linear regimes, their non-linear activations allow them—especially CNNs—to excel where linear methods fail. I compare AO performance using standard and CNN-based reconstructors through extensive simulations and optical-bench tests across varied conditions, magnitudes, and telescope configurations, including 8-m instruments (SPHERE+/VLT, SCExAO/Subaru) and ELT-class systems (MICADO/ELT). Results show that CNNs outperform linear reconstructors at high residual RMS, reducing or eliminating the need for modulation and yielding substantial sensitivity gains.

Items.Authors: Kohji Tsumura, Hideo Matsuhara, Koji S. Kawabata, Hiroshi Akitaya, Shuji Matsuura, Rinon Kageyama, Tomoya Hori, Haruaki Niinuma, Keisuke Shinozaki, Hiroshi Tomida, Akihiro Doi, Daisuke Yonetoku
Items.Title: Cryogenic optical test plan for the visible and near-infrared telescope MONSTER onboard HiZ-GUNDAM satellite
Items.Abstract: The HiZ-GUNDAM mission is dedicated to time-domain and multi-messenger astronomy focusing on gamma-ray bursts (GRBs). It is designed to deliver rapid alerts of high-redshift GRBs with photometric redshift provided by MONSTER, a 30-cm visible and near-infrared telescope onboard the satellite. After launch at ambient temperature, MONSTER is cooled to <200 K and its near-infrared detector to <120 K via radiative cooling, enabling high sensitivity in the near-infrared. The telescope employs an athermal design using a single aluminum alloy, ensuring uniform thermal contraction and stable image performance across temperatures. To validate this concept, a breadboard model (BBM) of MONSTER has been built for cryogenic optical testing. Beginning in April 2026, we plan to cool the BBM to operational temperature and conduct optical performance evaluations. This presentation summarizes the current development status of MONSTER, with emphasis on preparations for the BBM cryogenic optical tests.

Items.Authors: Yuan Li, Yasuhiro Hirahara, Ryoichi Koga, Umi Enokidani, Shunsuke Baba, Hideo Matsuhara, Takao Nakagawa, Takehiko Wada
Items.Title: Cryogenic transmittance measurements of large high-resistivity CdZnTe for immersion grating applications in the GREX-PLUS mid-infrared high-resolution spectrometer
Items.Abstract: We are developing a high-resolution mid-infrared spectrograph (HRS) with a cadmium zinc telluride (CdZnTe) immersion grating (IG) for the GREX-PLUS mission. The HRS aims to achieve a resolving power of R∼30,000 over 10–18 µm, requiring a high-index material with sufficiently low absorption at cryogenic temperatures. In our previous work, we demonstrated that high-resistivity CdZnTe (∼10^10 Ωcm) satisfies this requirement at ≤20 K. Building on this result, large (∼6 inch) CdZnTe ingots have recently been fabricated, enabling extraction of IG-sized blanks. We report new transmission measurements of 1 and 10 mm-thick samples cut near the extraction region of a large ingot with the same crystallographic orientation as the IG optical axis. The samples show a resistivity of ∼10^9 Ωcm. We also improved thermal stabilization of the measurement system and investigated the rapid increase in transmittance below ∼10 K, possibly due to freeze out of residual electrons.

Items.Authors: Pierpaolo Merola, Mauro Focardi, Vladimiro Noce, Marina Vela Nuñez, Marianna Michelagnoli, Simone Chiarucci, Gianluca Marotta, Elisabetta Giani
Items.Title: Cryo-harness shielding effectiveness assessment for ARIEL mission of the ESA’s Cosmic Vision Program
Items.Abstract: A simulation campaign has been carried out to assess the shielding effectiveness for the ARIEL mission. The analysis focuses particularly on the most sensitive cryo-cables, located outside the payload and the service module cavity. For all the instrument cable sets, conducted and radiated susceptibility analyses have been performed, including the evaluation of the transfer impedance (Zₜ). Time-domain analyses are also included to test the harness impulsive susceptibility and its response to transients. Special attention is given to the number of bonding connections and the maximum allowable resistance to the spacecraft reference ground. The simulation campaign has been performed using numerical electromagnetic analysis tools based on the Finite Element Method and Transmission Line Theory. The outcome of this study will be used to define appropriate reference requirements for the payload, ensuring that the harness design meets the necessary EM compatibility and performance.

Items.Authors: Yizheng Wang, Summer Luo, Jon Lawrence, Thierry Fusco, Benoît Neichel, Carlos Correia, Julien Charton, Pierre Jouve, Andrew Rakich, Andreas Seifahrt, Célia Blain, Gaetano Sivo, Jae-Woo Kim, Ho Seong Hwang, Masen Lamb, Martin Tschimmel, Dani Guzman
Items.Title: Culture is the key in international astronomical instrumentation projects: AAO-MQ experience from GNAO-AOB and K-SPEC
Items.Abstract: Australian Astronomical Optics at Macquarie University (AAO-MQ) develops advanced astronomical instrumentation within a setting that blends academic research with industry-grade project management and systems engineering. This paper highlights two major programs—the Gemini North Adaptive Optics Bench (AOB-WAN) and the K-SPEC spectrograph for KASI—to illustrate challenges and lessons from international, multi-partner collaboration. Experiences show that technical excellence alone is insufficient; project success depends on clear communication, shared expectations, and a strong, supportive team culture.

Items.Authors: Charles-Antoine Claveau, Hannah Gulick, Jessica R. Lu, Kodi Rider, Steven V. W. Beckwith, Josh Bloom, Sharon R. Jelinsky, Matt Dexter, Wei Liu, Dan Werthimer
Items.Title: CuRIOS-ED: optical AIT workflow and on-ground performance characterization of a 12U CubeSat imaging payload
Items.Abstract: CuRIOS-ED (CubeSats for Rapid Infrared and Optical Surveys – Exploration Demo) is a 12U CubeSat payload and pathfinder for the CuRIOS constellation, a fleet of CubeSats for optical monitoring of the transient sky. The payload combines a commercial Simera f/6 telescope with a Sony IMX455 CMOS detector in a custom camera housing. The system delivers a 3° field of view. We present the optical AIT workflow and on-ground performance of the telescope–detector assembly. A metrology-based alignment scheme positions the focal plane within the ±50 µm depth of focus, with a mean focus error <5 µm across the 36×24 mm sensor. End-to-end tests on a clean-room bench, using a custom OAP collimator, yield PSFs with core FWHM ≲1 pixel (<1.5″), consistent with the vendor wavefront map. PSF mapping after qualification-level vibration shows no measurable degradation, indicating that the CuRIOS-ED optical payload meets its image-quality budget and is robust against launch loads.

Items.Authors: Tomoya Hori, Koji S. Kawabata, Kohji Tsumura, Daisuke Yonetoku, Hideo Matsuhara, Shuji Matsuura, Hiroshi Akitaya, Akihiro Doi
Items.Title: Current development status of Kösters prism for MONSTER onboard HiZ-GUNDAM satellite
Items.Abstract: The concept of the HiZ-GUNDAM satellite is to search transients, including gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), with the wide-field X-ray monitor (EAGLE), and then perform autonomous follow-up observations of these objects using the visible and NIR telescope (MONSTER). The MONSTER adopts the Kösters prism for split NIR observation band 0.9-2.5μm into four bands and perform imaging observations simultaneously with a single NIR detector.  We have developed a double Kösters prism and are currently conducting tests and performance evaluations. As a performance evaluation, we tested cooling, irradiation and vibration resistance of adhesive using prism’s bonding points and we designed holding mechanism of prism and detector. Furthermore, we simply measured transmittance of each band of prism. I will describe on the development status and performance evaluation test results of the Kösters prism.

Items.Authors: Mehmet Kuruçolak, Ebru Uzunçam, Onur Şatır, Cahit Yeşilyaprak
Items.Title: DAG - HVAC control system: ventilation strategies for thermal performance of primary mirror on the DAG400 Telescope
Items.Abstract: In this study, the performance of the M1 cooling system components and optimization approaches for efficient cooling are presented. The impact of the DAG400 thermal management strategy on mirror seeing is quantified by comparing the full width at half maximum (FWHM) of stellar images obtained under three conditions: with the HVAC system operating, with only the ventilation doors open, and in a reference (no-cooling) configuration. In the analysis, FWHM is used as a performance metric sensitive to the total image degradation, including atmospheric, dome, and mirror-induced contributions, and the relative impact of different M1 cooling scenarios is evaluated using this metric. The results show that, in HVAC assisted cooling scenarios, the mirror seeing effect is reduced and the FWHM values can be significantly improved.

Items.Authors: Xinyu Yao, Jian Ge, Quanquan Hu, Yan Li, Jianqing Cai, Pengjun Zhang, Kevin Willis
Items.Title: Data analysis of laboratory photometry experiments with GSENSE 1081BSI CMOS Detectors
Items.Abstract: The Earth 2.0 (ET) mission, led by China, aims to detect over 50000 exoplanets, including potentially habitable Earth-like planets around Sun-like stars (“Earth 2.0s”), cold low-mass planets, and free-floating planets. The mission will employ six 28-cm telescopes to conduct ultra-high-precision photometric monitoring for the detection of transiting planets. To verify that the telescopes can reliably detect exoplanet transit events, we have developed a high-precision photometry testbed. This system evaluates selected CMOS detectors for their ability to detect Earth 2.0 transit signals, specifically those exhibiting photometric variations at the 84-ppm level. This report presents the laboratory data processing and analysis pipeline. Preliminary results show that, for simulated sources equivalent to a 12.5-mag Sun-like star, a photometric precision of 10 ppm can be achieved over a 6.5-hour timescale. Moreover, we have successfully recovered injected Earth 2.0-like transit signals.

Items.Authors: Mieke Bouwhuis, Karl Kosack, Maximilian Linhoff
Items.Title: Data processing and preservation for the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory
Items.Abstract: We present the data processing and preservation system for the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO). The CTAO is the next-generation very-high-energy gamma-ray observatory currently under construction at Paranal (Chile) and Observatory Roque de los Muchachos (La Palma, Spain). The data processing system handles the transfer of the petabytes of data generated by the Observatory and processes them into science-ready data products. The system also performs data qualification of low-level data from the Observatory and generates and processes simulation data required to model the instrument response. The data are processed in parallel workflows across different CTAO data centers and are managed at large scale at distributed locations. We describe the infrastructure used for preservation of the data and for execution of the data processing workflows.

Items.Authors: Dinko Milakovic, Guido Cupani, Bruce Bassett, Luca Pasquini, Stefano Cristiani
Items.Title: Data reduction methods for high fidelity spectroscopy
Items.Abstract: Testing potential variations of fundamental constants and measuring the cosmic expansion in real time demand extreme instrumental performance and control over systematic effects. Data reduction based on optimal extraction relies on simplifying assumptions about the instrument profile, that can distort the smallest spectroscopic signals. The spectro-perfectionism framework overcomes these limitations by forward-modeling the full two-dimensional instrument response and removing its imprint during extraction. We present the first application of this method to the ultra-stable HARPS spectrograph. Using HARPS’s laser frequency comb, we derive a highly accurate, spatially dependent model of its point-spread function, training an autoencoder to reconstruct its structure at subpixel resolution from thousands of comb lines across the detector. This example of a new generation of high-fidelity reduction pipelines is a pathway for achieving the precision required by future instruments like ANDES.

Items.Authors: Monique Cockram, Noelia Martinez Rey
Items.Title: Decreasing the solar exclusion angle for an event-based tip-tilt sensor in optical communications ground stations
Items.Abstract: Daytime adaptive optics faces additional challenges due to increased background noise and stronger atmospheric turbulence. With the rise in free space optical communications needing 24hr operation, current technologies face increased noise and signal errors. Conventional frame-based detectors are limited by the framerate and integration time, however recent event-based detectors are not. By only detecting changes in illumination in the field of view, each pixel asynchronously generates an event at each change. This high speed, low bandwidth data has also been demonstrated to have much lower shot noise during daytime operations. One limitation is the contrast between the signal and background, determined by angular distance to the sun and magnitude of the signal. We propose a method of artificially increasing the contrast of the event-based tip-tilt sensor, thereby increasing the sky coverage. On-sky testing of these methods demonstrated the advantages of artificial contrast generation.

Items.Authors: Andre P. Fogal, William Thompson, Christian Marois, Olivier Lardière, Joeleff Fitzsimmons, Kaitlyn Hessel, Adam Johnson, Christopher Mann
Items.Title: Deep learning wavefront reconstruction on-sky: results from the SPIDERS Lyot-based low order wavefront sensor
Items.Abstract: The Subaru Pathfinder Instrument for Detecting Exoplanets and Retrieving Spectra (SPIDERS) uses a Lyot-based Low Order Wavefront Sensor (LLOWFS) to perform pupil-plane wavefront sensing. Currently, wavefront reconstruction relies on a linear reconstructor, but this approach struggles with the inherently nonlinear nature of the problem, leading to instability and crosstalk between modes, adding additional signal that must be corrected by the LLOWFS. To address this, we have developed a machine learning-based wavefront reconstructor based on a convolutional neural network (CNN). The CNN is trained on SPIDERS bench data, increasing the linear range of the LLOWFS and leading to more effective wavefront control. We will present results demonstrating the CNN's performance in on-sky operation from the recent deployment of SPIDERS on the Subaru telescope. This approach is broadly applicable to low-order wavefront sensing and can help drive contrasts lower as we search for other worlds.

Items.Authors: Benedetta Di Francesco, Stefano Di Frischia, Ivan Di Antonio, Gianluca Di Rico
Items.Title: Deep learning wavefront sensing with multimode fibers : from numerical simulations to experimental implementation
Items.Abstract: The synergy between astronomy and photonics is offering new perspectives in the field of wavefront sensing for ground-based telescopes. In this context, the integration of photonic devices and machine learning is particularly promising. Within this framework, this research investigates the use of multimode fibers (MMFs) as wavefront sensors, combined with a properly trained Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). Aberrated wavefronts were propagated through a simulated multimode fiber with known properties, and the resulting intensity patterns were used for network training. Following this simulation phase, an optical bench has been developed to experimentally verify the concept and evaluate its performance under controlled laboratory conditions. This step marks a crucial transition from numerical modeling to physical implementation, enabling future developments and experimental validation.

Items.Authors: Camila Solar, Francisco Oyarzún, Jorge Tapia
Items.Title: Deep-learning-enhanced pyramid wavefront sensor in free-space optical communication scenarios
Items.Abstract: The rise of digital technologies demand high-fidelity, high-bandwidth communication systems. In this context, free-space optical communication (FSOC) emerges as an alternative to traditional radiofrequency (RF) links. However, atmospheric turbulence distorts the phase of the transmitted light signal. These distortions are corrected by adaptive optics (AO) systems which are based on the use of wavefront sensors (WFSs). In FSOC applications, the Shack–Hartmann wavefront sensor (SHWFS) is typically employed but owing to scintillation, it has problems in the phase-measuring process, risking quality of the coupling. In this work we evaluate the performance of the non-modulated pyramidal wavefront sensor (PWFS) under FSOC conditions and boost its functioning using deep learning tools. As a result, a comparison of the closed-loop performance of the SHWFS and PWFS will be presented using metrics related to FSOC and AO systems, aiming to explore the PWFS as a potential alternative for FSOC.

Items.Authors: Peyton Benac, Michael P. Fitzgerald, Eric Wang, Chris Johnson, Andrew J. Skemer, Philip Hinz, Nick MacDonald, Dale Sandford, R. Deno Stelter, Brittany Miles, Markus Loose, Richard Blank, Thomas Greene, Steph Sallum, William Deich, Dusty Reichwein, Aaron Hunter, Athira Unni
Items.Title: Demonstration of a hybrid fast/slow readout mode for the H2RG detectors in SCALES
Items.Abstract: The upcoming SCALES instrument for W.M. Keck Observatory will enable imaging and low-/mid-resolution coronagraphic integral field spectroscopic observations over 1-5 micron wavelengths, using two separate HgCdTe Teledyne Imaging H2RG detectors. These detectors are wired for slow-mode readout with 4 output channels at a pixel clock rate of ~100kHz, but when operated with a Teledyne Imaging SIDECAR ASIC followed by an AstroBlank/Markury Scientific MACIE controller card, the system can be operated at faster clock rates up to 1.8 MHz to avoid saturation on bright backgrounds—a mode referred to as hybrid fast-slow readout. We demonstrate cryogenic performance with the H2RG detectors in the complete SCALES instrument and characterize the detectors’ full-frame data acquisition performance in hybrid mode with pixel clock rates from 0.2-1.8 MHz. We present results obtained during detector system testing at UC Santa Cruz, and discuss next steps for commissioning and projected on-sky performance.

Items.Authors: Enrico Virgilli, Claudio Labanti, Lorenzo Amati, Giuseppe Baldazzi, Giuseppe Bertuccio, Edoardo Borciani, Riccardo Campana, Paolo Calabretto, Francesca Di Leo, Evgeny Demenev, Francesco Ficorella, Mauro Fiorini, Marco Grassi, Giovanni La Rosa, Piero Malcovati, Giulia Mattioli, Filippo Mele, Valerio Messina, Paolo Nogara, David Novel, Luca Nunziante, Giancarlo Pepponi, Paolo Sarra, Smiriti Srivastava
Items.Title: Design and characterization of the XGIS Detection Plane Demonstration Module (DPDM)
Items.Abstract: The X and Gamma-ray Imaging Spectrometer (XGIS) on THESEUS is designed to detect and localize transient X-ray and gamma-ray sources from 2 keV to 10 MeV, enabling high-resolution timing and spectroscopy for time-domain and multi-messenger astrophysics. It uses two identical coded-mask cameras imaging up to 150 keV and monitoring higher energies. The detection plane is built from thousands of modular elements, each a CsI(Tl) scintillator bar read by Silicon Drift Detectors (SDDs), offering broad-band coverage in a compact design. Recent developments include testing of SDDs and scintillator assemblies, ASIC prototype validation, and optimization of the electronic architecture, leading to the Detection Plane Demonstration Module (DPDM) developed by OHB-Italia with academic and research partners. This contribution presents the DPDM design, updated architecture, and performance tests within the THESEUS M7 Phase A.

Items.Authors: Hiroto Shimizu, Hikaru Munemura, Shohei Kusuda, Yuki K. Satoh, Hiroshi Nakajima, Koichi Hagino, Daiki Ishi, Masaki Numazawa, Yuichiro Ezoe, Kumi Ishikawa, Junko S. Hiraga
Items.Title: Design and development of focal plane CMOS camera onboard GEO-X (GEOspace X-ray imager)
Items.Abstract: We report the latest performance of the focal plane CMOS camera onboard the GEO-X (GEO-space X-ray imager) mission. The back-illuminated CMOS sensor has high sensitivity in the energy band from 0.3 to 2.0 keV and moderate energy resolution of 120eV (FWHM) at 0.6 keV. It is cooled down to -20 degC with Peltier cooler to reduce the dark noise. We have designed the camera body as a radiation shield and the vent pipe with the sufficient attenuation performance of intruding visible light. The developing status such as functional test including backend electronics and environmental tests will also be presented.

Items.Authors: Rodrigo Muñoz, Nicolas Hernández, Felipe Guzmán, Esteban Vera
Items.Title: Design and experimental implementation of deep holographic Fourier-plane wavefront sensors
Items.Abstract: We present the design and experimental implementation of deep holographic Fourier-plane wavefront sensors for astronomy and free-space optics. Pyramid-like Fourier elements are encoded as low-cost holograms by computing their phase, generating an off-axis computer-generated hologram, and recording it from an SLM onto a holographic plate with a 4f system. On the bench, an SLM generates atmospheric phase screens with controlled r0, while the holographic Fourier sensor measures the distorted wavefront. A transformer neural network is first trained on simulated data and then refined with a mix of simulated and experimental images, learning a mapping from sensor images to Zernike modal coefficients. In closed loop, the SLM acts as a turbulence generator and an ALPAO deformable mirror provides correction. We report residual wavefront error and Strehl ratio for different turbulence strengths and discuss chromatic response and diffraction efficiency as key limitations for future improvements.

Items.Authors: Eduardo Medinaceli Villegas, Natalia Auricchio, Donata Bonino, Vito Capobianco, Mauro Dadina, Sebastiano Ligori, Mauro Focardi
Items.Title: Design and functionalities of the instrument control unit of the newAthena's X-IFU instrument
Items.Abstract: ESA's NewAthena mission proposal is under development and will undergo mission adoption in 2027. This general-purpose open X-ray observatory of the Hot and Energetic Universe will have an unprecedented combination of collective area, survey capabilities and energy resolution provided by the X-ray Integral Field Unit (X-IFU) instrument.  Here, the current preliminary design of the Instrument Control Unit (ICU) hardware and application software of X-IFU is presented. The ICU is part of a very complex SpaceWire network, the avionics architecture dealing with data harvesting, data buses and data handling, which defines the instrument capabilities, is governed by the ICU. The main ICU role is to handle all the data and generate the commands required onboard. It uses both a high-speed bus and a PPS signal to orchestrate the control of the instrument. All ICU functionalities will be implemented in the ASW running in the state-of-the-art processor, based on a preemptive multi-task architecture.

Items.Authors: Qi Feng, Hong-fei Zhang, Baolong Chen, Qiang Wu, Zi-yi Liu, Jian Wang
Items.Title: Design and progress of the CMOS Mosaic Camera for Earth 2.0's microlensing telescope
Items.Abstract: The Exoplanet Earth Science Survey Satellite (Earth 2.0) is planned to be deployed in a halo orbit around the Sun–Earth L2 point. It will function as a space observatory consisting of six wide - field transit telescopes and one microlensing telescope. By combining the transit and microlensing methods, it will conduct a large - scale survey of terrestrial planets and free - floating planets. The microlensing CMOS camera is assembled from four 9K×9K detectors tiled together with guiding detectors. When combined with high - precision thermal control and readout electronics, it can achieve highly stable photometry with a single - exposure signal-to-noise ratio ≥ 5 for targets of 20.5 magnitude. The relevant key technologies have been validated using a prototype camera, which demonstrates that they meet the requirements of both scientific observations and engineering implementation.

Items.Authors: Chenlong Li, Hualin Chen, Jiaxin Li, Hua Bai, Dehua Yang
Items.Title: Design of a conical phase optical system for RINGSS
Items.Abstract: This paper presents a conical phase optical system for the Ring-Image Next Generation Scintillation Sensor (RINGSS). By introducing a virtual phase compensation surface in front of the telescope, two rear configurations are developed: a rear air-spaced spherical lens group that generates an approximate conical phase by combining the 11th Zernike polynomial coefficient (spherical aberration) with telescope defocus, and a rear axicon based on the first-order term of an odd-order aspheric surface to produce an exact conical phase. Both systems deliver high-quality, achromatic ring images over the 400–800 nm wavelength range, with effective half-fields of view of 1 arcminute (approximate design) and 3 arcminutes (exact design), respectively. The enhanced RINGSS system will be deployed for site monitoring of China’s Large Optical/Infrared Telescope.

Items.Authors: Yu Ning, Hao-ran Ma, Wen-qing Qu, Shao-zhen Zhu, Hong-fei Zhang, Jian Wang
Items.Title: Design of a low readout noise InGaAs camera based on high-speed digitalization scheme for astronomical application
Items.Abstract: Short-wave infrared (SWIR) imaging offers strong atmospheric transmission, low background noise, and stable day–night performance, making it highly valuable in astronomy, precision measurement, and industrial inspection. InGaAs detectors, featuring low dark current, modest cooling requirements, good linearity, and cost advantages, have become the mainstream SWIR focal-plane technology. In this work, a low-readout-noise and high-speed digitalized SWIR camera system is developed using a 640×512/15 μm InGaAs focal-plane array from the Kunming Institute of Physics. The system integrates TEC cooling, precision bias circuitry, FPGA-based timing control, and a high-speed readout chain consisting of a low-noise preamplifier, a wide-bandwidth differential ADC driver, and a 16-bit 250 MSPS ADC. Imaging tests, photon-transfer-curve (PTC) measurements, dark-current characterization, and noise evaluation confirm the system’s overall performance,

Items.Authors: Song-hao Li, Hang Zhan, Qi Feng, Xingbo Wang, Zi-yi Liu, Hong-fei Zhang, Jian Wang
Items.Title: Design of sCMOS Test Camera and its Radiation Test for Aerospace Applications
Items.Abstract: The harsh space radiation environment poses significant challenges to the reliability of detector systems, making the on-orbit validation of high-performance and robust CMOS image sensors a critical step for aerospace applications. We will present the design and systematic radiation testing of a prototype system based on the GSENSE1517BSI, a large-format, back-illuminated CMOS detector, developed for such demanding environments. To evaluate its performance and radiation tolerance, we developed a prototype camera and conducted a series of tests, including proton and Co-60 γirradiation experiments under biased, low-temperature operating conditions, followed by annealing studies. We will detail the electronics of the camera and summarize test results of key parameters—such as gain, bias, readout noise, dark current, quantum efficiency, and full-well capacity—before and after irradiation, as well as after annealing.

Items.Authors: Hui Zhang, Bixuan Zhao, Xinyu Yao, Hongjing Yang, Wei Chen, Chenliang Huang, Maochun Wu, Jian Ge
Items.Title: Design of the ground data processing and operations segment for the ET (Earth 2.0) mission
Items.Abstract: The ET mission will deliver unprecedented time-domain data sets for exoplanets and stellar astrophysics: six 28-cm transit telescopes downlink full-frame images at 15-minute cadence and postage stamps for selected targets, while a 35-cm microlensing telescope returns 10-minute cadence imaging toward the Galactic bulge. With a total data rate of 2500Gb per day and survey scales of >5 million FGKM dwarfs and >30 million bulge stars, the Ground Data Operation Segment (GDOS) is a critical element that transforms raw telemetry into validated science products and provides reliable, timely access for the community. This paper presents: (1) a science-driven requirements analysis; (2) the end-to-end ground processing flows for both the transit telescope array and the microlensing payload; and (3) the design framework for the science database and user service platform.

Items.Authors: Fabio D'Anca, Michela Todaro, Ugo Lo Cicero, Luisa Sciortino, Gabriele Minervini, Enrico Bozzo, Philippe Peille, Elise Bellouard, Sebasten Clamagirand, Gael Parot, Edoardo Cucchetti, Lander Ruiz de Ocenda, Daniele Brienza, Elisabetta Cavazzuti, Marco Barbera
Items.Title: Design of the New Athena X-IFU thermal filter supporting the technology readiness assessment
Items.Abstract: The NewAthena mission's X-ray Integral Field Unit (X-IFU) uses four thermal filters (THFs) to attenuate infrared and radio-frequency radiation from the spacecraft environment and to protect the cryogenic detector from particulate contamination, and to attenuate UV/Vis light from astrophysical sources. All these functions must be ensured while maintaining high X-ray transparency. During phases A and B, extensive studies have been conducted to optimize the mechanical design and to characterize the technology by environmental testing, demonstrating robustness for space applications. The investigations involved two membrane types: polyimide and carbon nanotube (CNT). This work presents the mechanical design of the THFs for the technology readiness assessment, along with preliminary results from FEM analysis and experimental testing. These developments represent a key step toward achieving the Technology Readiness Level 5 (TRL5) required for the subsequent phases of the Athena mission.

Items.Authors: Michael Gonzales, Andrew Skemer, R. Deno Stelter, Nicholas MacDonald, Basil Blank, Gerald Cabak
Items.Title: Design, construction, and testing of the SCALES cryostat
Items.Abstract: SCALES (Slicer Combined with an Array of Lenslets for Exoplanet Spectroscopy) is a 2–5 µm high-contrast, fully cryogenic integral field spectrograph and imager designed for operation behind the adaptive optics system at the W. M. Keck Observatory. The SCALES cryostat provides the stable, low-background environment required for high-sensitivity exoplanet characterization. It houses a large optomechanical payload cooled by two closed-cycle cryocoolers, with an internal liquid-nitrogen tank used to accelerate bench cooling at the start of each cooldown. This paper presents the assembly, pumpdown, and cryogenic tests of the SCALES cryostat, starting with an initial empty-cryostat run to validate vacuum integrity, thermal performance, and procedures. Subsequent cooldowns with progressively added mechanisms and optics achieved stable vacuum and an average bench temperature of about 80 K, demonstrating robust, repeatable performance that supports ongoing integration for future use at Keck.

Items.Authors: Sorabh Chhabra, Stefan Kraus, Jyotirmay Paul, Daniel Lancaster, Narsireddy Anugu, Michael J. Ireland, John D. Monnier, Owain Snaith
Items.Title: Design, integration, and commissioning of the BIFROST All-in-One 4-telescope Beam Combiner for 1.0–1.8 μm spectro-interferometry
Items.Abstract: The ASGARD/BIFROST instrument provides spectro-interferometric capability for the VLTI across the 1.0–1.8 μm wavelength range. Central to this system is the All-in-One (AIO) 4-telescope beam combiner, which integrates beam routing, spatial filtering, and spectrograph injection within a compact optomechanical assembly.  We present the optical and optomechanical design of the AIO combiner. The assembly and laboratory integration procedures are summarized, with emphasis on metrology, throughput verification, and fringe stability tests. Commissioning at the VLTI is reported with initial on-sky performance, including beam alignment, fringe acquisition, visibility calibration, and sensitivity across the Y–H bands.

Items.Authors: Dongok Ryu
Items.Title: Design-to-as-built distortion modeling of Korsch Telescopes for weak-lensing surveys
Items.Abstract: Weak gravitational lensing requires highly accurate galaxy shape measurements, making geometric distortion a critical systematic in wide-field space telescopes. Korsch TMAs offer excellent low-order aberration control but struggle to achieve the low distortion needed for weak-lensing surveys. This work addresses this challenge via three integrated approaches. First, a machine-learning framework identifies low-distortion solutions within wide-field Korsch design space. Second, an end-to-end observation model based on non-sequential ray tracing simulates intrinsic galaxy structure, weak-lensing shear, optical propagation, and pixel sampling in a unified 3D environment. Third, as-built mirror poses from an Integrated Metrology System generate a realistic distortion model. Comparing ML-derived designs and as-built data enables clearer separation of instrumental distortion from true gravitational shear, supporting distortion-controlled telescope development for future weak-lensing missions.

Items.Authors: Malhar Sonaniskar, Douglas Neill, Ellie Hileman
Items.Title: Determining stress based bending mode limits for the LSST M1M3 active mirror system
Items.Abstract: The LSST M1M3 primary-tertiary mirror, an 8.4m actively supported by 156 pneumatic actuators, requires precise stress prediction for safety during surface correction. Assuming linear proportionality between stress-strain and strain-displacement, we developed a rapid stress-estimation method: combining the peak stresses of the first 20 unit bending (Zernike) modes via RSS (Root Sum Square). This combined RSS stress prediction was validated with FEA (Finite Element Analysis) using NASTRAN. This approach enables instantaneous peak stress safety checks for actuator force optimization in real-time telescope operation. This paper details the formulation, workflow, validation, and practical application of this RSS-based stress prediction for LSST M1M3 active optics.

Items.Authors: Natasha Carr, Charly H. Feldman, Simon T. Lindsay, Adrian Martindale, Will Dunn, Bryn Parry, Jonathan Nichols, Sam Wharton, George Clark
Items.Title: Developing a novel in-situ X-ray telescope for a Jovian mission
Items.Abstract: The Jovian system provides a multitude of X-ray sources, including emissions from the diffuse radiation belt and Io plasma torus, atmospheric and auroral emissions and plasma-surface interactions with the Galilean moons. In-situ observations will provide fluxes in the range of 104-106 ph/s, allowing for full characterisation of X-ray emissions.  We present an X-ray instrument concept for a Jupiter mission. The 6 x 6 MPO array and 630mm focal length provides a 19 degree field-of-view and a <1000km resolution at 5 Jupiter radii. This concept draws on the extensive history and heritage of lobster eye telescopes developed at the University of Leicester.
